clue.text: Pirate Hannay's creator talked of incessantly to poets

indicators.note: a thing talked of is spoken, so the name before it is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: John Buchan wrote the Richard Hannay thrillers, starting with The Thirty-Nine Steps
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always or incessantly

explanation.surface: A thriller writer is supposedly forever going on to poets about pirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked of' makes BUCHAN, the name of the novelist, sound like BUCCAN; the poets' E'ER completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a seventeenth-century Caribbean sea robber, so the word is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Loyal companion champion's taken around Panama, for example

indicators.note: the champion's word is wrapped round the next piece, as the clue says it is taken around it

parts.note: an ace is a champion, and the 's reads as 'is', giving aces
a Panama is a kind of straw hat

explanation.surface: A loyal friend of a champion is escorted round Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country but is the hat; the 's of champion's gives the plural ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates is the faithful friend of Aeneas in Virgil, and his name became a byword for a devoted friend.

clue.text: Person who's worried, perhaps, about aircraft controller?

parts.note: one who ails is troubled or unwell, playfully called an ailer
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone anxious is fretting over air traffic control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aircraft controller' suggests an air traffic controller, but it is a hinged flap on a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a movable surface on a wing that controls the roll of an aeroplane.

clue.text: Eg a pledge the Spanish spelt out

parts.note: a vow is a solemn pledge
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone spells out a pledge, with a Spanish article thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelt out' tells the solver that the letter in the definition is meant as a letter: the A of the alphabet is one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is one of the five letters of its class, alongside E, I, O and U.

clue.text: Passing a couple of poles, I plunged into river

indicators.note: the pieces dive into the river's name, so they sit inside it

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Travelling past a pair of poles, someone dives into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient is passing or fleeting, lasting only a short while.

clue.text: Deterioration concerning northern Scandinavians, reportedly

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a business letter

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the people's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the Lapps are the people of Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A decline is being blamed on the people of the Arctic north, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes LAPPS sound like LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into worse health after improvement, a deterioration.

clue.text: Very old duke keeps active at first: that's the spirit!

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words before this phrase are used

explanation.surface: An ancient aristocrat stays energetic, and someone cheers him on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's the spirit!' reads as encouragement but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear distilled spirit, so the exclamation points straight at it.

clue.text: Crowd in ferry port runs almost to the front

indicators.note: the letter for runs travels forward but stops one place short of the very start

parts.note: Dover is the Kent port for cross-Channel ferries
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A crowd in a busy port rushes nearly to the front of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost to the front' moves the R of DOVER up to second place, giving DROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd or moving throng, so it can mean a crowd, as in droves of people.

clue.text: Naval commander unknown to be so trite

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
RN is the Royal Navy
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is so unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: Corny means hackneyed or banal, the same as trite.

clue.text: Capital excessively used to tour the Bluegrass state

indicators.note: touring goes round something, so the first word surrounds the state

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much
Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State, is abbreviated KY

explanation.surface: A city overused for tours of Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Lovingly protect companion quietly leaving to die

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: the quiet letter departs from the word for die

parts.note: to perish is to die
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A friend slips away silently to die, cared for tenderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the P from PERISH, leaving ERISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish is to hold dear and care for tenderly.

clue.text: County once reached by hiker with rosy disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the two words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A cheerful walker arrives at a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals the rearrangement. Yorkshire, England's largest historic county, was split up in 1974, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire was a single county of northern England until local government reform divided it.

clue.text: Old railwaymen given points to look after

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now merged away
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Retired railway workers are told where to look after things.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to care for or tend someone, the same as looking after them.

clue.text: Quick note about joint of meat

parts.note: brisk means quick or lively

indicators.note: about turns the note round so it is read backwards

parts.note: te is the seventh note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A hasty message about a roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TE to ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, a joint for roasting or braising.

clue.text: Dominance by select group? Priest's first to moan about it

annotationWithheld.why: Dominance by select group? Priest's first to moan about it: the only parse found is ELI'S + M (first to moan) round IT reversed (TI), where 'about' must both contain and reverse, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Dominance by select group? Priest's first to moan about it

clue.text: Former prison bosses initially show competence on horseback

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: to show competence on horseback is to ride well

explanation.surface: Managers show good horsemanship at an old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name came to mean any house of correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, originally a London jail, became a general term for a house of correction.

clue.text: Fine specimen sometimes put before queen?

definitions.meaning: a fine example or something lovely is called a real ...
the word pairs with queen to make the title of a pageant winner

explanation.definitionFit: A beauty is a fine example of something, and the beauty queen is a pageant winner.

clue.text: Nab individual pinching key part of skeleton

indicators.note: pinching holds something tightly between, so the key sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: to collar someone is to nab or arrest them
one means a single individual
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A policeman nabs a single person who is stealing a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft but signals that the key letter sits in the middle of the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone, or clavicle, is a bone of the shoulder girdle in the skeleton.

clue.text: A Native American holding silicon to be frictional

indicators.note: the warrior's word holds the element symbol within it

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: A warrior carries a chip of silicon that rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive means causing wear by rubbing, so it describes something producing friction.

clue.text: Male sea eagle circling island

indicators.note: the eagle's name goes round the island letter

parts.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle

explanation.surface: A cock eagle wheels around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' looks like a description of the bird but defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's name, a pet form of Ernest, so it is an example of a male.

clue.text: People with dog in Brands Hatch, perhaps

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: Spectators bring their dog into Brands Hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: Brands Hatch is a motor-racing circuit in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Brands Hatch is a motor-racing circuit, an example of a course for races.

clue.text: Scoop journalists will ultimately spread around coastal resort

indicators.note: the two end letters are spread apart to go round the resort's name
only the final letters of the two words before it are taken

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton on the Sussex coast

explanation.surface: Reporters will eventually swarm a seaside town for an exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoop' looks like a news exclusive, but it is the digging tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a broad-bladed tool for scooping up earth or coal.

clue.text: Pack taken from Inverness to Wick

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Luggage is taken along from Inverness up to Wick.
explanation.walkthrough: Inverness and Wick are towns in the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack things away neatly.

clue.text: Old instrument foreign spy used to secure change

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next word fast within them
foreign suggests something strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: An overseas agent uses an antique instrument to force a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' makes PSY, which 'to secure' wraps round the word for change.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient plucked stringed instrument of the zither family.

clue.text: Shellfish — one consumed by a friend of Pickwick

indicators.note: the numeral is swallowed by the surrounding pieces

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day
Nathaniel Winkle is one of Mr Pickwick's companions in Dickens's novel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Dickens character eats something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' reads as the article, but means per.
explanation.definitionFit: The periwinkle is a small edible sea snail, a shellfish.

clue.text: Woman loses head, barmy about Bacchanalian song

indicators.note: the woman's name drops its opening letter

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name

indicators.note: about suggests moving things round, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazed woman goes on about a drunken song.
explanation.walkthrough: EDITH less its head is DITH; 'about' rearranges BARMY to YRAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was a wild choral hymn to Dionysus, or Bacchus, the god of wine.

clue.text: Slow to a trot, as it were, seeing source of drink

definitions.text: Slow to a trot, as it were
definitions.meaning: a horse that goes from canter down to trot is playfully said to ...
a glass vessel from which wine or port is poured

explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is the stoppered glass vessel that wine is poured from, while the jokey verb means reducing a canter.

clue.text: Prisoner's anger about initiator of Popish Plot?

indicators.note: the prisoner and anger pieces surround the single letter

parts.note: a con is a convict; the 's makes cons
ire is anger

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word starts it

explanation.surface: A convict fumes over the man behind the Popish Plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Popish Plot was a fabricated 1678 conspiracy against Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot together in secret.

clue.text: Where Juan possibly lives, in the same place up river

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place in references

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A Spaniard lives in the same place upriver.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan is a typical Spanish name, so he lives on the peninsula of Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal, where a man called Juan would plausibly live.

clue.text: Chaste woman's way to cut meat

indicators.note: the street abbreviation cuts into the meat

parts.note: veal is calf meat
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman's method of carving meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestal virgin was a priestess of Vesta sworn to chastity, so a chaste woman.

clue.text: Spiritual leader's ban upset bishop on island

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: to bar is to ban
B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A clergyman's prohibition overturns a bishop on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader.

clue.text: Order regularly observed in leading article?

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is looked at

explanation.surface: A command is followed in the main newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading article' suggests an editorial, but it is a strap that leads a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap by which a horse is led and guided, so it is a leading article.
